uncited: *   **Input:** A set of candidate training views (with camera poses) and the current state of 3D Gaussian primitives (position, covariance, opacity, spherical harmonics coefficients) after a specified number of training iterations.
*   **Coverage Feature Map ($V_{max}$):** A 2D image buffer with the same resolution as the target rendering.
Each pixel stores a scalar value representing the maximum direction-dependent coverage of Gaussian primitives.
*   **Candidate Views:** A list of camera poses excluding the currently selected training views and the reserved evaluation views.
*   Select one fixed view as the first training view.
*   Select three additional views by maximizing the Euclidean distance to the camera centers of the existing views.
*   Continue training until the iteration count reaches the threshold for the next view selection.
*   Calculate the mean value across all pixels of the rendered map.
*   Select the candidate view with the **lowest** mean value.
This corresponds to the view with the lowest overall coverage from already selected views.
*   Add the selected view to the training set.
*   Repeat until 20 training views are reached.
This adds computational overhead proportional to the number of candidates and the resolution of the feature map.
